title: Non-Visual Effects of Light on Melatonin, Alertness and Cognitive Performance: Can Blue-Enriched Light Keep Us Alert?
research_question: To investigate if commercially available compact fluorescent lamps with different colour temperatures can impact on alertness and cognitive performance, specifically if blue-enriched light (6500K) induces greater melatonin suppression and enhanced alerting effects compared to warmer light (2500K, 3000K).

participants.description: Sixteen healthy young men (age range: 20-28 years; mean 24.3±2.1 SD) recruited from Swiss universities. Participants were non-smokers, free from medical, psychiatric, and sleep disorders (PSQI score <5), and without extreme chronotype ratings.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Three different light settings in a uniformly painted room (high reflective white painting, acting as an integrating sphere) at 40 lux illuminance at eye level (12 cd/m2 luminance): 1. Compact fluorescent lamp (CFL) with 6500K CCT (blue-enriched). 2. Compact fluorescent lamp (CFL) with 2500K CCT (warm comfort light). 3. Incandescent lamp with 3000K CCT (classic light). All lamps were 18W. Spectral compositions were similar above 530 nm, but 6500K had considerably higher output between 420-520 nm. Exposure duration was 2 hours in the evening.

measures.instrument: Derived from VAS mood, tension, and physical comfort
Visual Comfort Scale (VCS) subscales ('Does the light have less glare or more?' and 'Is the light too dark or bright?')

measures.construct: Sustained attention and response control (reaction time)

mechanisms: Non-image-forming (NIF) photoreceptive pathway, primarily involving melanopsin-containing intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs), mediates the circadian and direct effects of light.
The retino-hypothalamic tract connects ipRGCs to the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), which in turn influences the pineal gland (melatonin regulation) and projects to arousal-regulating brain areas.
Light irradiance signals reach the SCN, then the locus coeruleus (LC) in the brainstem, triggering thalamic activity and widespread modulation over cortical activity, enhancing sustained attention.
Cone photoreceptors may also contribute to non-visual responses at the beginning of light exposure and at low irradiances, while melanopsin is primary for long-duration/high irradiance exposure.
Enhanced activation in the sustained attentional network is modulated by the non-visual system via melanopsin.
implementation_implications: The selection of commercially available compact fluorescent lights with different colour temperatures significantly impacts circadian physiology and cognitive performance at home and in the workplace.
Blue-enriched light settings can provide an effective rationale for enhancing alertness and performance.
Blue-enriched light may be useful in the treatment of circadian rhythm sleep disorders, such as shift work disorder.

limitations: The study was conducted under stringently controlled conditions, which may limit the generalizability of findings to more practical, real-world scenarios.
Only male volunteers were included, limiting the generalizability of results to females.
No apparent benefit was observed for higher executive cognitive tasks (PVSAT), suggesting a limited scope of cognitive improvement.
The luminance level of 40 lux was relatively low, which might not be sufficient to elicit all potential alerting effects.
